title: How HashMap works internally

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (2 of 2)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: HashMap is an array of buckets. A key's hash code, spread with the high bits mixed in, selects the bucket. Each bucket holds a linked list of entries. When the number of entries exceeds capacity times load factor (0.75 by default), the table doubles and entries are redistributed. Since Java 8, a bucket with many collisions (eight or more, with a large enough table) turns into a red-black tree, so lookup worst case is O(log n) instead of O(n). Keys need consistent equals and hashCode.

points.title: Bucket selection
points.why: The hash picks a bucket index, and collisions are chained inside that bucket.

points.title: Resize at load factor
points.why: Growing at 0.75 keeps buckets short, so lookups stay fast.

points.title: Treeify on collisions
points.why: Long chains become red-black trees, which limits the worst case under attack.
